Done. All five assigned items are closed with normative recipes and executable reference cases.

## What was corrected

**M1 — `subjectScopeCommitment`.** The recipe is `"sha256:"` + the 64 hex of `H("subject-scope", D)` — the *same digest* as the foundation `scope2` identity, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` form. No native H domain, no second preimage. `D` is the closed foundation `subject-scope` record over the host's own exhaustive enumeration. Implemented at the admitted producer boundary (`admit_coverage_result_v3`) and at coverage use (`coverage_view_use`); the host mints `scope2` *before* reading the payload's commitment, so no claimant digest is authority. Acyclic: closures → context → universe → scope2 → commitment → coverage2 → view2. The C-2 artifact is untouched; its `SHAPE ONLY` deferral stays a historical non-recipe. Identity §3 converged on the same wording independently during the session.

**M2 — TypeScript native context.** `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`) plus ten supporting defs, carrying `typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` at the same nesting as `rustcDevLlvmDigest`, with per-field producing recipes and whole retained stdlib/compiler trees. A Rust descriptor offered as a TypeScript context refuses. A2 is a three-form encoding table in §11; A1 fixes both citations.

**M5 — public detail vocabulary.** The de-facto rule is now normative (S12.1): base code before the first colon is the `DomainDetailCode`, the rest is `subject`, D9 branch from the refusal, closed 191-member set with no wildcard family. `PROFILE_SET_KEY_NOT_MACHINE_ID` is a *subject* of `NT-TCB-PROFILE-UNQUALIFIED`, not a code. **11 codes for Codex** (two more than the reviewer found — the sweep caught `ROOT.TR_REPAIR_THRESHOLD_POLICY` / `ROOT.TR_PROFILE_THRESHOLD_POLICY`) plus one internal alias; all 11 proven to refuse today and admit after registration.

**S2** names `RootV1`/`RootV2` in the successor bundle as the sole admission boundary, with newline-suffix regressions through `admit_root_document`. **S6**: all six "(obligation, Codex)" notes were already discharged; the prose now names implementing functions and asserting checks. Zero remain.

## Results

| Checker | Result |
|---|---|
| native | PASS 132/132, 60 cells, 0 open objects |
| security | passed, 456/456, 10/10 sweeps |
| integration | 327 passed, 0 failed |

Six mutation runs confirm the new guards bite. I also fixed a pre-existing cross-unit regression: Codex's tightened canonical-set admission was failing `default_capability_selection` — a live instance of the M-3 item Codex owns.

**Codex's coauthor note.** It found seven real defects in my draft — including the one that mattered most, that I had left `context` optional in `bind_typescript_universe`, which preserved the exact bypass the check exists to close. All seven are fixed with regressions; `context` is now required with no weaker admit path.

Two notes on limits: the foundation launcher is pin-blocked in the working tree from concurrent edits (parallel-integration drift, not a design issue — I repinned nothing), and none of this is product, native, OS or crypto qualification. Handoff at `/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/blind-corrections-author.v1/handoff.{md,json}`. Coauthor only, not self-accepted; these are successor edits and need a newly frozen subject.
